# Agent Taskbay

> Agent Taskbay is a self-hosted, open-source human-in-the-loop (HITL) operations console for AI agents and Agent2Agent (A2A) workflows. It provides durable task persistence, selective human approval gates, multi-modal artifact review, and append-only audit logging.

## Core Facts & Quickstart

- **Type**: Self-hosted web application & background task worker runtime.
- **License**: MIT (Created by Shashi Kanth G S, part of Allsrc).
- **Default Port**: Web Console binds to `http://127.0.0.1:3002` (local embedded PGlite database).
- **Sample Agents Port**: Demo fixtures bind to `http://127.0.0.1:4010`.
- **CLI Commands**:
  - `npx agent-taskbay` — Starts the web console on port 3002.
  - `npx agent-taskbay demo-agent` — Starts five reference sample agents on port 4010.
- **Protocol**: Standard [A2A (Agent2Agent) Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org).
- **Documentation**: [https://taskbay.allsrc.dev](https://taskbay.allsrc.dev)
- **GitHub Repository**: [https://github.com/allsrc/agent-taskbay](https://github.com/allsrc/agent-taskbay)

## Architecture

- **State Durability**: Commands and task events are committed to the local embedded database (PGlite) or PostgreSQL before being dispatched. When the browser closes, tasks continue running in background workers.
- **Single Source of Truth**: The browser never connects directly to autonomous agents and never holds agent credentials. The UI reads the database; background workers communicate with agents via HTTP streaming, push callbacks, and polling.
- **Safe Multi-Modal Artifacts**: Previews text, Markdown, JSON, CSV, PNG/JPEG, audio, video, and PDF artifacts using fixed, sandboxed renderers without executing agent-supplied code.
- **Separation of Duties & Revision Locks**: Human approval decisions are bound to the exact content revision proposed by the agent. If the task state shifts or expires, the decision is rejected.

## Protocol & Agent Card Schema

Any autonomous agent can connect to Agent Taskbay by publishing an Agent Card JSON at `/.well-known/agent.json` or `/card.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "Production Deployer",
  "description": "Orchestrates database migrations and infrastructure rollouts.",
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:4010/deployer",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "capabilities": {
    "extensions": [
      "https://a2a-protocol.org/ext/approval-request/v1",
      "https://a2a-protocol.org/ext/structured-form/v1"
    ]
  },
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "deploy",
      "name": "Deploy Application",
      "description": "Trigger an environment deployment requiring human review."
    }
  ]
}
```

### Task Lifecycle States
1. `submitted`: Created and enqueued in Taskbay database.
2. `working`: Agent accepted task and is executing.
3. `input-required`: Agent needs structured parameters or answers from a human operator.
4. `auth-required`: Sensitive action requires authenticated human sign-off (with optional high-risk warning).
5. `completed`: Final artifacts generated and task resolved.
6. `failed` / `cancelled`: Terminated or operator-cancelled.

## Framework Integrations

- **LangGraph**: Use Taskbay as an out-of-process interrupt queue for sensitive tool invocations. Instead of pausing a long-running Python thread in memory for hours, emit an A2A task with an approval gate and resume upon callback.
- **Google ADK (Agent Development Kit)**: Route `LongRunningFunctionTool` and `require_confirmation=True` actions through Taskbay. The agent hibernates its `RunState` (0% CPU/RAM allocated) until a signed, revision-locked approval is delivered by the human operator.
- **CrewAI**: Wrap sensitive tools with an approval check against Taskbay. The agent pauses, waits for the signed human review, and continues execution with the approved parameters.
- **Python Agents**: Publish an HTTP endpoint serving an Agent Card and dispatching status updates to Taskbay.
